title: Pixelproof run record v1
description: `run.json` — the single source of truth for whether a run is open (ADR 0009 §2), versioned by ADR 0014. Unknown fields are tolerated on read at this major; an unknown major is refused. Every path is relative to the run directory, POSIX-separated, so an archived or remounted run directory stays readable.

accepted.description: A projection of `state`, never an independent field: true only in `accepted`, null in `running`, false everywhere else — which is ADR 0009 §4's explicit `accepted: false` while pending.

resolved.description: Resolved spec, provider, judge and environment decisions. Its presence is stable; its interior is a diagnostic bag and is not versioned (ADR 0014 §3). ADR 0020 §4 reads `prompt`, `provider`, `size` and `retakes` back out of it to build attempt n+1, which is exactly why the original prompt is recorded here at generate time and costs nothing to add.

retakes.description: The attempt bound this run was opened with: `--retakes`, else `spec.retakes`, else 1 (ADR 0020 §6). Honoured only inside a judged run.

prompt.description: The original prompt, before spec folding. Null on a run that had none, such as one opened by `verify --judge host`.

attempts.description: Ordered by `number` ascending, starting at 1 and contiguous.

outcome.description: Null until the run reaches a terminal state.

reasons.description: Named, recorded refusals and outcomes. Codes are stable; the prose is not.

judge.description: ADR 0009's handoff record, written when a run is judged. The authoritative per-check verdict table lives in `checks`: on escalation a round-2 verdict REPLACES the round-1 one for that check rather than joining a panel with it, and `escalatedFrom` records that it happened. Absent on a run that asked for no judge.

kind.description: Who judges this run. `host` is a run state answered by a later `judge submit` (ADR 0009 §1); `subprocess` is a judge spawned and answered inside one invocation, so the run never enters `pending-judgement` and never exits 2 (ADR 0021 §3); `mixed` is both. Widened in place from `{"const": "host"}` at major 1 (ADR 0021 §5): the field keeps its name and its string type and "host" keeps its meaning. Treat it as an OPEN ENUM — a consumer that switches on it needs a default arm.
kind.$comment: The three values are pinned by test/judge-registry.test.mjs so a fourth cannot arrive unnoticed.

panel.description: The authorities that judged this run, in the order `--judge` named them. Absent on a run written before ADR 0021, where `kind: "host"` said everything there was to say about who was judging.

trust.description: `builtin` or `external` for a judge adapter (ADR 0004); `host` for the calling agent, which ADR 0009 classifies as neither.

round.description: The run-wide round number the verdict came from. Rounds do not restart per attempt (ADR 0020 §5), so this is not bounded at 2; the two-round bound is per attempt and lives in `rounds[].attempt`.

rounds.description: ADR 0009's escalation rounds, in issue order. The open round is the last entry whose `submittedAt` is null; a run in `pending-judgement` has exactly one. Bounded at two rounds PER ATTEMPT — there is no round 3 for an attempt. Round numbers do not restart per attempt (ADR 0020 §5): attempt 1 uses rounds 1 and possibly 2, attempt 2 starts at round 3, which keeps `judge-request-<round>.json` unique inside one directory.

attempt.description: Which attempt this round judges. Absent on rounds written before ADR 0020, where it is 1 because only one attempt could exist.

submittedAt.description: Null while the round is unanswered. An unanswered round is never a pass.

cache.description: Reserved for ADR 0015. Not written by this phase.

runId.description: Equals the run directory's basename. The time separator is a hyphen because a colon is not a legal Windows filename character (ADR 0009 §2).

state.description: Closed within this major. `accepted`, `rejected` and `abandoned` are terminal: a closed run is never reopened, which is what makes ADR 0009's nonce single-use.

timestamp.description: ISO-8601 UTC. Precision beyond whole seconds may change.

relativePath.description: Relative to the run directory, `/`-separated, never absolute and never escaping upward.

sha256.description: Of the bytes in the run directory after the copy, so the digest describes the file a later reader opens.

skipped.description: Carried separately from `passed` forever: a skipped check is not a passed one.
